content.text:
### enum_declaration node type and fields

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php_only/src/node-types.json

Definition of the enum_declaration node from the PHP grammar's generated node-types.json. Its fields are: attributes (attribute_list), body (required enum_declaration_list), and name (required name); children include class_interface_clause and primitive_type (the enum backing type).

```json
  {
    "type": "enum_declaration",
    "named": true,
    "fields": {
      "attributes": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": false,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "attribute_list",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "body": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": true,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "enum_declaration_list",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "name": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": true,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "name",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "children": {
      "multiple": true,
      "required": false,
      "types": [
        {
          "type": "class_interface_clause",
          "named": true
        },
        {
          "type": "primitive_type",
          "named": true
        }
      ]
    }
  },
```

--------------------------------

### PHP class, interface, trait, enum declarations with constants

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/test/corpus/bugs.txt

Shows the expected parse tree for a PHP file containing class, interface, trait, and enum declarations with various constant declarations, including visibility modifiers and primitive types.

```s-expression
(program
  (php_tag)
  (class_declaration
    name: (name)
    body: (declaration_list
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration
        (const_element (name) (integer))
        (const_element (name) (integer))
        (const_element (name) (integer))
        (const_element (name) (integer))
        (const_element (name) (integer))
        (const_element (name) (integer)))
      (const_declaration
        (visibility_modifier)
        type: (primitive_type)
        (const_element (name) (string (string_content))))))
  (interface_declaration
    name: (name)
    body: (declaration_list
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (string (string_content))))))
  (trait_declaration
    name: (name)
    body: (declaration_list
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (string (string_content))))))
  (enum_declaration
    name: (name)
    body: (enum_declaration_list
      (const_declaration (const_element (name) (boolean))))))
```

--------------------------------

### class_declaration fields in node-types.json

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php/src/node-types.json

The class_declaration entry in node-types.json shows its only fields: attributes, body, and name. Notably there is no parent_class, base_classes, or interfaces field — those names do not exist anywhere in this grammar.

```json
  {
    "type": "class_declaration",
    "named": true,
    "fields": {
      "attributes": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": false,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "attribute_list",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "body": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": true,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "declaration_list",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      },
      "name": {
        "multiple": false,
        "required": true,
        "types": [
          {
            "type": "name",
            "named": true
          }
        ]
      }
    },
```

--------------------------------

### class_declaration rule definition

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js

The grammar rule for class_declaration: it defines the field 'name' (plus 'attributes' and 'body'), and uses optional base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) nodes instead of parent_class/base_classes/interfaces fields. Method declarations appear inside the body's declaration_list, and functions are named function_definition in this grammar.

```javascript
      class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(
        optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)),
        repeat($._modifier),
        keyword('class'),
        field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)),
        optional($.base_clause),
        optional($.class_interface_clause),
        field('body', $.declaration_list),
      )),
```

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/test/corpus/declarations.txt

Shows an interface declaration and a class that implements it, along with the corresponding parse tree. The interface method has a visibility modifier and the class includes a property and method.

```php
<?php

interface ThrowableInterface {
    public function getMessage();
}

class Exception_foo implements ThrowableInterface {
    public $foo = "foo";

    public function getMessage() {
        return $this->foo;
    }
}
```

```s-expression
  (interface_declaration
    name: (name)
    body: (declaration_list
      (method_declaration
        (visibility_modifier)
        name: (name)
        parameters: (formal_parameters))))
  (class_declaration
    name: (name)
    (class_interface_clause
      (name))
    body: (declaration_list
      (property_declaration
        (visibility_modifier)
        (property_element
          name: (variable_name

        parameters: (formal_parameters)
        body: (compound_statement
          (return_statement
            (member_access_expression
              object: (variable_name
                (name))
              name: (name))))))))
```

aptu-coder

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) code-intelligence server that gives AI coding agents pre-parsed symbol tables instead of raw file bytes, cutting token usage by up to 59% in the cited benchmark conditions (see Benchmarks). OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search).
